# C02 — justification

Every semantic unit of `slice-crew.md`, why it exists, what breaks without it, whether it could be shorter, and where it comes from. The artifact is 35 lines; the table has 34 units plus 11 deliberate omissions.

| 2 | “C02 buys one thing” | Sets a single outcome and blocks scope growth. | The crew becomes a second production team. | “One outcome” is shorter but weaker. | SRC5, SRC6 |
| 3 | “a slice a stranger can finish” | Defines done from the player's side, not the builder's. | The crew ships a demo only its author can complete. | No. | SRC3, SRC4 |

## Deliberate omissions

1. Agent role prompts — owned by A01–A04.
2. The nine S10 points in full — owned by S10; this file names the count and the build order.
3. The D07 template — owned by D07/S09.
4. The S09 tuning protocol — owned by S09.
5. The R9 budget arithmetic — owned by R9.
6. The R8/G1 fun criteria — owned by R8/G1.
7. The G2 decision text — owned by G2.
8. The capture command — owned by CLI10.
9. Project build commands — owned by `project.config.json` (N00).
10. The stranger script — owned by S10.
11. Release/store checklist — owned by S13.

## Known tensions

- “Settings” is in the build list but not one of the nine DoD points; it is part of the menu frame, not a tenth check.
- A02 writes the D07 note but does not run sessions; A01 runs them. This is deliberate: observation and interpretation are separate.
- “No second review” applies after the critic closes; a G2 `fix` sends only the named points back for one round.
